record.original_question: For a graph G, let chi_l(G) be the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L admits a proper L-coloring, and let chi*_l(G) be the least integer k such that for every k-list-assignment L, the graph G admits an L-packing of size k, meaning k pairwise-disjoint L-colorings. Does there exist a graph G for which the list packing number exceeds the list-chromatic number by at least 2, that is, chi*_l(G) > chi_l(G) + 1?

evidence.quote: The list-chromatic number (or choosability) chi_l(G) of a graph is the minimum integer k such that every k-list-assignment L admits an L-colouring. Given a k-list-assignment L of G we call a collection of k pairwise-disjoint L-colourings an L-packing of size k, or less specifically a list-packing. The list packing number chi*_l(G) of G is the least k such that G admits an L-packing of size k for any k-list-assignment L of G.
Problem 2.1 Is there a graph G for which chi*_l(G) > chi_l(G) + 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. A $k$-list-assignment on $G$ is a function $L$ that assigns to each vertex $v\in V$ a set $L(v)$ of $k$ colors. A proper $L$-coloring of $G$ is a map $f:V	o igcup_{v} L(v)$ such that $f(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v\in V$ and $f(u)
e f(v)$ whenever $uv\in E$. The list-chromatic number $\chi_\ell(G)$ is the least integer $k$ such that every $k$-list-assignment of $G$ admits a proper $L$-coloring.

Given a $k$-list-assignment $L$ of $G$, an $L$-packing of size $k$ is a collection $\{f_1,\dots,f_k\}$ of proper $L$-colorings of $G$ that are pairwise disjoint in the sense that $f_i(v)
e f_j(v)$ for all $v\in V$ and all $1\le i<j\le k$. The list packing number $\chi_\ell^*(G)$ is the least integer $k$ such that for every $k$-list-assignment $L$ of $G$, the graph $G$ admits an $L$-packing of size $k$.

Question: Does there exist a graph $G$ for which
$$\chi_\ell^*(G) \;>\; \chi_\ell(G) + 1\,?$$

status_evidence.title: A Short Proof that the List Packing Number of any Graph is Well Defined
status_evidence.snippet: Studies list packing number; well-definedness established but bounds vs. list-chromatic number remain a key open direction.
status_evidence.claim: The gap between list packing and list chromatic numbers is an active open question.

status_evidence.title: List packing number of bounded degree graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates upper bounds on χ*_l(G); known examples only achieve χ*_l(G) = χ_l(G)+1 in certain cases.
status_evidence.claim: Whether χ*_l(G) can exceed χ_l(G)+1 is open.

artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether some graph satisfies $\chi_\ell^*(G) > \chi_\ell(G) + 1$ appears in recent literature on list packing as an open problem. Searches did not surface a published example achieving a gap of at least 2, and recent works continue to address bounds relating these two parameters, suggesting the problem remains open.
